page: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-128 is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to the Memory Optimized machine family. It delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 platform operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity reaches 3904 GB, resulting in approximately 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, while GPU hardware and bundled local disks are absent.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate distinct performance boundaries between single-threaded and parallel workloads. Multi-threaded execution scores in the upper tier, recording 120,764.87 on stress-ng multi-core and 17,456.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In contrast, single-core metrics remain average, with stress-ng reaching 1844.19 and Geekbench scoring 1576.0. Memory throughput is robust, showing 298.34 GB/sec on large read blocks and 123.31 GB/sec on large write operations. The architecture achieves top-tier results in cryptographic calculations with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 103,896.01, alongside 106.82 million Redis SET operations per second and strong static web serving throughput.

Because the configuration lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, all persistent I/O relies on attached network volumes, and large-scale deep learning text generation scales poorly, as seen in the 2.73 tokens per second result on 70B language models. From an operational efficiency perspective, the machine consolidates extreme working sets into a single NUMA domain, reducing the overhead of distributed memory clusters for memory-bound tasks. The instance is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory data warehousing, and intensive transactional ETL pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-128 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.6 GHz and 3904 GB of RAM. Designed for extreme in-memory requirements, it offers an expansive 30.5 GB of RAM per core alongside AVX-512 vector support and robust cryptographic extensions. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile multi-threaded processing, reaching 120,764.87 on stress-ng and 17,456.0 on Geekbench multi-core, while single-core performance settles in the mid-range. Memory bandwidth reaches 298.34 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting over 106 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance contains no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage requires attached network volumes, and large model text generation remains constrained. The configuration is primarily matched to enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale data caches, in-memory analytics, and memory-intensive ETL batch workloads.
